{
  "question_intent": "Clarification on NII growth and the impact of hedging",
  "main_topics": ["NII growth", "Hedge impact", "Future NII dynamics"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",

  "question_quote": "The only thing I would add is that, on your Slide 10, you show £1.2 billion of additional revenue from the hedge and yet if I'm looking at your guidance, banking NII is not going to grow by £1.2 billion, it's going to be somewhat less than that. So that would sort of imply that despite all the volume growth, the underlying NII, if it wasn't for the hedge, we wouldn't be getting really any NII growth at all. And I'm just thinking about what that means as we go beyond this year and into sort of '28, '29, '30, what's happening in terms of the underlying dynamics?",

That is somewhat enhanced by the fact that our deposit stability is there, and therefore it's important that we grow the deposit franchise also. The thing I would also say is look back over the last few quarters, Ed, and add up what's coming in from the asset balance column in BUK, and you will see that you are getting to a building momentum of asset income. I think you'll get to like £130 million to £140 million of additional income coming through in BUK alone on that metric. Clearly that is just building quarter in, quarter out. It's somewhat being led by mortgages, so the margin's going to be a little bit lower than BUK as a whole. If you go into corporate, it's exactly the same, the NII growth in corporate is being driven by lending as much as it's being driven by deposits. data.question_intent: Clarification on NII growth and the impact of hedging
data.question_quote: The only thing I would add is that, on your Slide 10, you show £1.2 billion of additional revenue from the hedge and yet if I'm looking at your guidance, banking NII is not going to grow by £1.2 billion, it's going to be somewhat less than that. So that would sort of imply that despite all the volume growth, the underlying NII, if it wasn't for the hedge, we wouldn't be getting really any NII growth at all. And I'm just thinking about what that means as we go beyond this year and into sort of '28, '29, '30, what's happening in terms of the underlying dynamics?
data.answer_quote: Well, I mean, this is clearly the gross hedge income. The other thing I would say is, there is momentum from the structural hedge, we know that. That is somewhat enhanced by the fact that our deposit stability is there, and therefore it's important that we grow the deposit franchise also. The thing I would also say is look back over the last few quarters, Ed, and add up what's coming in from the asset balance column in BUK, and you will see that you are getting to a building momentum of asset income. I think you'll get to like £130 million to £140 million of additional income coming through in BUK alone on that metric. Clearly that is just building quarter in, quarter out. It's somewhat being led by mortgages, so the margin's going to be a little bit lower than BUK as a whole. If you go into corporate, it's exactly the same, the NII growth in corporate is being driven by lending as much as it's being driven by deposits. And this is really important for the long-term balance of NII. Of course, at the moment, this is being disproportionately driven by the structural hedge, but at some point in the future, beyond 2028, it's really important that the diversification within NII comes through, and those asset balances start to carry that momentum from there on in. That's what we're very much focused on. Thank you. Next question, please.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the question's concern about NII growth and the role of hedging, providing specific figures and a forward-looking perspective.
